minutes.headline: Assessors approved four sets of backlogged minutes, got a revaluation kickoff update, and set a closed January 22 meeting to sign exemptions.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors caught up on minutes (April 4, October 11, November 20, December 4), signed a motor vehicle commitment, invoices and the third-quarter estimated tax commitment, and heard the interim principal assessor's report on the revaluation kickoff with Vision and staffing. Long discussions covered resident questions on lakefront property cards, senior exemption options, condo land valuation, the website and "how to read your Vision card" materials, and ad hoc citizen committees. The board scheduled a focused January 22 meeting and then entered executive session.

public_comment.topic: Asked about the online Vision cards showing added percentages for lakefront properties, whether 2023/2024 card data and past abatements will be used by the revaluation contractor, when inspections occur, and how the public will be told how assessments are set before tax bills.
Chair asked for closing public comment; none was offered.

votes.motion: Accept the recreated minutes of April 4, 2023

Accept the amended November 20 minutes with 'Master' project plan inserted
Enter executive session under the cited chapter 59 section 60 purpose (abatement and exemption applications)

budget_items.what_was_said: The commitment covered abatements issued on a number of vehicles and the board signed it.

budget_items.topic: Third quarter estimated real estate tax commitment
budget_items.what_was_said: The third quarter commitment is a share of the prior estimated bills, with the first two quarters already paid. New growth and actual adjustments come in the fourth quarter.
A folder of unsigned invoices had accumulated during the principal assessor's absence; the board signed them for review with the finance staff.
Eligible seniors have used up their hours for the year and the program restarts January 1. HR may supply temporary help if the principal assessor remains out.
The state questioned new growth because it had doubled; a spreadsheet of new homes and a large commercial building satisfied them.

budget_items.topic: Budget request for part-time data collector
budget_items.what_was_said: Board agreed to suggest to the town manager that next year's budget fund a part-time data collector.
Discussion of the existing 41C exemption amount and the possible 41C and a half option, which would need town meeting action and would not affect this tax year.
Dispute over how condo land is valued; one complex sale was averaged per unit.

decisions.decision: Staffing recommendations will go on the January 8 agenda, then to the town manager for the budget; the interim assessor and a member will work up the task allocation.
A focused closed meeting to sign exemptions and chapter land applications will be held January 22, location to be determined.
Ad hoc citizen committee proposal will return to the next meeting for in-depth review of ground rules and which tasks citizens can do.
A member will check with the software vendors on how often the CAI cards can be updated and recommend a frequency.
The interim assessor will investigate whether a town can adopt more than one senior exemption; the board believes only one.
No vote taken on the possibly unheld June 7 meeting; board treated it as done.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors scheduled a closed meeting on January 22 to sign exemptions and chapter land applications; the location was not set.
The board approved four sets of backlogged minutes and signed a motor vehicle commitment, backlogged invoices and the third-quarter estimated real estate tax commitment.
The interim principal assessor reported on the revaluation kickoff and staffing, and the board agreed to suggest funding a part-time data collector in next year's budget.
Staffing recommendations will go on the January 8 agenda and then to the town manager for the budget.
The board deferred the proposal for ad hoc citizen committees to its next meeting, and the interim assessor will look into whether a town can adopt more than one senior exemption.

why_it_matters: The revaluation sets the values that property tax bills are built on, and the staffing request would go into next year's town budget, so both can affect what residents pay and how quickly questions about their assessments get answered.
Whether a second senior exemption option (called 41C and a half in the meeting) is possible would need town meeting action, so it is a vote residents could later be asked to take.
